title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
description: Foundational paper introducing the general Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture combining pre-trained parametric memory (BART seq2seq model) with non-parametric memory (Wikipedia dense index accessed via DPR dual-encoder). Compares RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token generation formulations.

title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
description: Pioneering retrieval-augmented pre-training method that treats document retrieval as a latent step inside masked language modeling. Demonstrates end-to-end backpropagation through a Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) retrieval module with asynchronous document index updates.
concepts: dense neural retriever training without explicit supervision

title: Improving Language Models by Retrieving from Trillions of Tokens
description: Introduces RETRO (Retrieval-Enhanced Transformer), scaling retrieval augmentation to language models trained on massive corpora (trillions of tokens). Uses chunk-level cross-attention to incorporate retrieved text into the autoregressive transformer decoding process.
concepts: frozen BERT embeddings for passage representation
computational efficiency in large LM training

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
description: Seminal work establishing that dual-encoder dense representations trained with simple contrastive loss and in-batch negative sampling outperform classical BM25 lexical retrieval for open-domain question answering across multiple benchmarks.
concepts: FAISS indexing for fast vector search

title: Unsupervised Dense Information Retrieval with Contrastive Learning
description: Presents Contriever, an unsupervised dense retrieval model pre-trained solely via contrastive learning on raw text spans using inverse cloze task and data augmentation strategies. Demonstrates strong out-of-domain transfer on the BEIR benchmark without supervision.

title: The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond
venue: Foundations and Trends in Information Retrieval
description: Comprehensive treatise on the Okapi BM25 probabilistic relevance framework. Formulates the core mathematical theory of term frequency saturation, inverse document frequency (IDF), and document length normalization parameters (k1, b).

title: SPLADE v2: Sparse Lexical and Expansion Model for Information Retrieval
description: Introduces SPLADE v2, a learned sparse retrieval model that maps queries and documents into sparse high-dimensional term representations aligned with vocabulary logits. Overcomes BM25 vocabulary mismatch via neural term expansion while maintaining inverted-index efficiency.
concepts: L1 / FLOPS regularization for sparsity control

title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion Outperforms Condorcet and Individual Rank Learning Methods
description: Foundational ranking fusion paper establishing Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). Demonstrates that summing reciprocal ranks (1 / (k + r)) across distinct retrieval runs is robust, hyperparameter-resilient, and consistently outperforms score-based rank learning and Condorcet voting.

title: Pyserini: A Python Toolkit for Reproducible Information Retrieval Research with Sparse and Dense Representations
description: Presents an authoritative framework unifying sparse (Lucene/BM25) and dense (Faiss/HNSW) retrieval. Establishes the standard experimental methodology for hybrid linear score fusion (alpha * dense + (1 - alpha) * sparse) and reproduction protocols.
concepts: first-stage retrieval efficiency vs accuracy trade-offs

title: Passage Re-ranking with BERT
description: Seminal cross-encoder re-ranking paper applying deep bidirectional Transformers to passage ranking. Demonstrates that feeding concatenated query-passage pairs into full self-attention layers yields state-of-the-art re-ranking accuracy at higher latency.

title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
description: Introduces the late-interaction paradigm for information retrieval. Precomputes token-level contextualized passage embeddings and scores queries via a fast MaxSim operator, achieving cross-encoder-like precision with orders-of-magnitude lower latency.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
description: Introduces reflection tokens to train an LM that autonomously decides when to retrieve passages, evaluates retrieved passage relevance, and assesses its own generation for factual grounding and utility.

title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation
description: Introduces Corrective RAG (CRAG) to improve robustness against inaccurate retrieval. Employs a lightweight retrieval evaluator with confidence thresholds (Correct, Ambiguous, Incorrect) to trigger document strip decomposition, web search fallback, or document filtering.
concepts: web search fallback for low-confidence retrieval

title: Adaptive-RAG: Determining When and How to Retrieve for Knowledge-Intensive Tasks
description: Focuses directly on dynamically routing queries according to complexity. Employs a small classifier trained on LLM-generated reflection traces to dynamically dispatch queries across No-Retrieval, Single-Hop Retrieval, and Multi-Hop Retrieval pipelines, optimizing efficiency and accuracy.
concepts: No-Retrieval vs Single-Hop vs Multi-Hop pipelines
classifier training from LLM reflection traces
